decisions.evidence: Round 2, maker entry 3 asks whether preserving an actual copy is essential or a bonus/later item. Client entry 4 says: “Preserving a copy is important to me, but I’d treat it as a later addition.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly identifies the preservation expectation and accepts deferring it from the first version; requirements stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 2, maker entry 3 offers one combined “keep it but not in my face” concept versus separate read-soon and reference stashes. Client entry 4 selects separate mechanisms: “Read later is an active queue” and archiving has “a separate place where I can find and restore them.”
decisions.note: The offered combined alternative would not fulfill the reference distinction; the client selects the conforming separation at requirements discovery.

decisions.evidence: Round 2, maker entry 3 asks whether the main view should show unread items, everything, or recent saves. Client entry 4 selects “recent, non-archived saves—not only unread items.”
decisions.note: The client selects a reference-conforming default collection with unread items available separately; requirements stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7 presents pasting a URL and pressing Save link, with the saved item appearing immediately. Client entry 8 says: “The save action feels quick.”
decisions.note: The presented basic URL-save behavior conforms; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7 presents “a single ‘Recent’ list, newest at the top.” Client entry 8 approves the new link appearing at the top but does not identify the absence of user-selectable sort keys.
decisions.note: A fixed newest-first list does not provide the reference’s ability to sort by a chosen key; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7 states: “Each saved item shows three things: a title, the web address underneath, and when it was saved.” Client entry 8 discusses the guessed title but not the absent description, tags, or favicon.
decisions.note: The explicitly enumerated card content omits reference-required list information; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7 says it “guessed a title automatically from the address.” Client entry 8 rejects this: “The guessed title from the address isn’t good enough” and asks for the page’s real title automatically.
decisions.note: The client replaces URL-derived guessing with reference-conforming page-title collection; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, maker entry 7 asks whether the client would want to type a title while saving. Client entry 8 instead requests automatic collection “with a way for me to change it if needed.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing ability to edit an automatically collected title; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5, maker entry 9 presents the real page title filling in automatically after saving. Client entry 10 says: “Yes, that matches what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Automatic collection of the real title is conforming; revised prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, maker entry 11 offers rename interactions while retaining a way to open the original URL. Client entry 12 selects the pencil/in-place editor and says: “I want clicking the title to open the original page.”
decisions.note: After-save title editing and navigation to the original URL are both represented; prototype choice review.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, maker entry 13 offers folders allowing exactly one location versus multiple tags per link. Client entry 14 selects tags because “A link often belongs to several categories.”
decisions.note: The folders alternative would violate many-to-many tagging; the client selects the conforming tags alternative.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, maker entry 13 presents filtering through top-row and per-link tag chips. Client entry 14 says both kinds of tag chips “work well for browsing.”
decisions.note: Selecting a tag filters to that tag’s bookmarks as required.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, maker entry 13 presents entering comma-separated tags without suggestions. Client entry 14 adds: “I’d also like to see existing tag names suggested as I type.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing existing-tag autocomplete requirement; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, maker entry 15 presents matching existing-tag suggestions while saving. Client entry 16 says the suggestions make it easy to keep tags consistent.
decisions.note: The revised autocomplete behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, maker entry 15 presents filtering from either the Browse row or a bookmark’s tag. Client entry 16 calls both straightforward.
decisions.note: Both presented tag-selection paths conform to tag filtering.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, maker entry 17 instructs the client to type lowercase “java” to match the seeded “JavaScript | MDN” item. Client entry 18 approves the search behavior.
decisions.note: The demonstrated differing-case match is conforming evidence for case-insensitive search.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, maker entry 17 defines search over title, address, and tags. Client entry 18 explicitly states the difference: “If links later have descriptions or my own notes, I’d expect those to be searched too,” while accepting the current behavior.
decisions.note: The client surfaces the missing description/note search coverage but frames it as applying when those later fields exist, accepting the first-version departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, maker entry 17 presents search narrowing within the active tag. Client entry 18 says this combination is helpful provided the selected tag remains visible.
decisions.note: Combining tag and text constraints with AND-like narrowing conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, maker entry 19 presents an opt-in “Read later” action and says new links are not queued automatically. Client entry 20 explicitly approves opt-in behavior.
decisions.note: The bookmark can be marked unread/read-later as required.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, maker entry 19 presents a dedicated To read tab containing only queued items. Client entry 20 says this matches the intended queue.
decisions.note: The separate unread-only view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, maker entry 19 presents Mark read removing an item from the queue while retaining it in All. Client entry 20 explicitly confirms that meaning.
decisions.note: Marking read removes the bookmark from the unread view without deleting it.

decisions.evidence: Round 11, maker entry 21 presents archived links hidden from All, To read, and normal search. Client entry 22 says: “This is the right behavior.”
decisions.note: Archive hides bookmarks from default and ordinary search views as required.

decisions.evidence: Round 11, maker entry 21 presents a separate Archived tab with its own search and tag filtering. Client entry 22 explicitly approves it.
decisions.note: The separate archive view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 11, maker entry 21 presents one-click archive and restore as reversible actions. Client entry 22 approves because “the action is reversible.”
decisions.note: The presentation preserves the required distinction between reversible archive and permanent deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, maker entry 23 presents editing a bookmark’s title and tags together through the pencil form. Client entry 24 selects that form.
decisions.note: The presented title-and-tag editing operations themselves conform; prototype choice review.

decisions.evidence: Round 12, maker entry 23 describes the all-in-one edit form as containing “the title and all tags together.” Client entry 24 approves it without asking to edit the URL, description, or note.
decisions.note: As the presented whole-bookmark editor, it omits other fields required by REF-BM-04; prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 13, maker entry 25 says the main prototype now has the “full ‘edit this bookmark’ form (title + tags with suggestions).” Client entry 26 says the behavior sounds right and does not surface the absent URL, description, or note fields.
decisions.note: The revised main-prototype editor remains narrower than the reference; integration review.

decisions.evidence: Round 13, maker entry 25 asks whether permanent delete should exist at all. Client entry 26 selects the conforming alternative: “Yes, I do want permanent delete.”
decisions.note: The offered no-delete alternative would diverge; the client selects permanent removal.

decisions.evidence: Round 13, maker entry 25 contrasts permanent delete with reversible archive. Client entry 26 asks that deletion be clearly distinguished from archiving.
decisions.note: The presented distinction conforms and is reinforced by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 14, maker entry 27 presents permanent deletion, including from Archived, behind a confirmation that points to Archive as the reversible alternative. Client entry 28 accepts the behavior.
decisions.note: Permanent deletion and its distinction from archive conform; revised prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 prevents duplicate saves and provides Show it for the existing bookmark, including archived ones. Client entry 30 says this is preferable because “From there I can edit or restore it.”
decisions.note: Guiding the user to the existing editable bookmark is functionally equivalent to the duplicate-save rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, maker entry 29 blocks clearly invalid text while accepting ordinary hostnames and filling in https. Client entry 30 approves this strictness.
decisions.note: The URL validation and normalization are compatible with URL-based saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 16, maker entry 31 presents long text wrapping, multi-line tags, and normal scrolling. Client entry 32 says: “The layout holds up for me.”
decisions.note: This readability/layout aspect of the list conforms, independent of the earlier missing-field divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 16, maker entry 31 proposes still saving when title retrieval fails and temporarily using the URL as the editable title. Client entry 32 says this is “exactly right.”
decisions.note: Graceful fallback for an unreachable title does not contradict automatic collection when available.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, maker entry 33 gives the complete first-version scope as collecting “the page’s real title” and separately places descriptions later; it does not collect description, favicon, or preview image. Client entry 34 broadly approves the first-version scope without identifying those missing metadata fields.
decisions.note: The specification-gate metadata scope is narrower than REF-BM-02.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, maker entry 33 limits editing to “title and tags together via the pencil” and lists descriptions/notes as later. Client entry 34 approves without surfacing absent pre-save editing or URL/description/note editing.
decisions.note: The specification-gate editor omits required editable fields and before-save editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, maker entry 33 specifies multiple tags and matching existing-tag suggestions. Client entry 34 says the summary captures the settled first version.
decisions.note: The specification-gate tagging and autocomplete decisions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, maker entry 33 specifies browsing by either the top tag row or a bookmark’s tag. Client entry 34 approves the settled scope.
decisions.note: The specification-gate tag-filter behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 client entry 18 had explicitly stated that future descriptions and notes should also be searched. Round 17 maker entry 33 scopes current search to titles, addresses, and tags and defers descriptions/notes; client entry 34 accepts this as the first version settled on.
decisions.note: The linked specification-gate disposition explicitly defers fields whose expected searchability the client had already stated.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, maker entry 33 summarizes opt-in To read, the queue-only view, and Mark read removing items while keeping bookmarks. Client entry 34 approves the scope.
decisions.note: The specification-gate read-later behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, maker entry 33 summarizes hidden/restorable archived bookmarks, a separate archive, and confirmed permanent deletion. Client entry 34 approves the scope.
decisions.note: The specification-gate archive and delete decisions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 client entry 4 explicitly calls preservation important but a later addition. Round 17 maker entry 33 records “saving a full copy of each page” for later, and client entry 34 approves the first-version scope.
decisions.note: This is the specification-gate confirmation of the client’s explicit, accepted deferral of snapshots.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, maker entry 33 explicitly places “per-link notes/descriptions” outside the version being built. Client entry 34 gives general approval but does not itself state and accept the markdown-note/rendering requirement.
decisions.note: The note capability is expressly deferred, but bare scope approval does not qualify as an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, maker entry 35 reports implemented saving where “the real page title fills in” and again records per-link descriptions for later; no description, favicon, or preview-image collection is presented. Client entry 36 broadly accepts the approved first version.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the described metadata implementation remains narrower than REF-BM-02; execution is not inferred beyond the presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, maker entry 35 reports the implemented editor as “the title-and-tags form” and records descriptions/notes for later. Client entry 36 accepts without identifying absent URL/description/note editing or before-save editing.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation retains the specification-gate editor divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, maker entry 35 reports multiple tags, normalization, tag browsing, and existing-tag suggestions. Client entry 36 accepts the application.
decisions.note: The implemented tagging, filtering, and autocomplete presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 client entry 18 explicitly expected future descriptions/notes to be searched. Round 18 maker entry 35 reports current search only across titles, addresses, and tags and records those fields for later; client entry 36 says the later additions are “recorded appropriately.”
decisions.note: The implementation-review response accepts the previously explicit deferral of broader full-text fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, maker entry 35 reports the opt-in queue, queue-only view, and Mark read behavior. Client entry 36 accepts the application.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation for read-later conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, maker entry 35 reports hidden archived items, a separate archive with restore, and permanent confirmed deletion. Client entry 36 accepts the application.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation for archive and delete conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, maker entry 35 reports duplicates prevented and the existing item surfaced even when archived. Client entry 36 accepts the application.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation conforms to duplicate convergence and guidance.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 client entry 4 explicitly accepted preservation as a later addition. Round 18 maker entry 35 records “saving a full page copy” for later, and client entry 36 says the later additions are recorded appropriately.
decisions.note: Implementation-review confirmation of the explicitly accepted snapshot deferral.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, maker entry 35 records “per-link notes” for later. Client entry 36 refers generally to later additions but does not itself express and accept the reference’s markdown-note and rendering expectation.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation expressly omits notes; the response is insufficient for accepted_divergence under the bare-approval rule.
